newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-ANDERLECHT DOWN BUT NOT OUT AFTER JINX YEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANDERLECHT DOWN BUT NOT OUT AFTER JINX YEAR.

text.p: Match-fixing allegations, a ban of their leading striker, injuries, humiliating defeats -- Belgian Cup finalists Anderlecht had a jinxed season.
But the proud Brussels side are determined to end their 'annus horribilis' on a positive note by beating Ekeren in the Sunday's final.
"If we win the Cup the season would still be acceptable for Anderlecht," club president Roger Vanden Stock said.
Away from the pitch, UEFA has been investigating match-fixing allegations related to the 1984 UEFA Cup semifinal against England's Nottingham Forest.
Anderlecht were allegedly blackmailed by two men who claimed to have bribed the Spanish referee of the 1984 game.
The affair have tarnished the image of Belgium's most prestigious club, which has constantly denied the allegations.

Another blow came from Belgium striker Gilles De Bilde when he broke the nose and eye socket of an opponent by punching him in a league game in December. De Bilde was immediately banned. Soon afterwards he moved to Dutch PSV Eindhoven.
Virtually every Anderlecht player has been hit by injuries and the rejuvenated team, which had seen a handful of regulars quit last season, had some embarrasing defeats.
"It's been a difficult season with many ups and down," Swedish international midfielder Par Zetterberg said.
The last defeat Anderlecht remembers all too well.
A hat-trick by Canadian Tomasz Radzinski led Ekeren to a humiliating 4-1 win, Ekeren's first and only league victory over Anderlecht in more than six years.
Ekeren coach Herman Helleputte was quick to rub salt in Anderlecht's wounds.

"Anderlecht are still a good team, but on a lesser day they can lose to a number of teams, us for instance. If we have a good day and they don't, we win. This year they are vulnerable," Helleputte said.
"It's now or never," said Belgium and Ekeren goalkeeper Philippe Vande Walle. "But with Ekeren you never know. It could be 4-0 but also 0-4."
Anderlecht, who clinched four league titles in the past seven years, narrowly qualified for next season's UEFA Cup only seven minutes from time in the final match last Sunday.
"The pressure is off," Zetterberg said.
But management, anxious to polish up Anderlecht's tarnished reputation, badly want to beat Ekeren and qualify for the more prestigious Cup Winners' Cup for their 38th European campaign.
Anderlecht should not underestimate Ekeren, who have scored 21 goals in their five latest league matches and won them all.
"Our strikers can make the difference...(Radzinski) weighs constantly on defence," Ekeren coach Herman Helleputte said.
"We also have the psychological edge after we beat them with such a big difference," he said.
But Anderlecht midfielder Bruno Versavel, who is moving to Italian side Perugia, is determined to deny Ekeren.
"I want to show my gratitude for all the faith they put in me when I had to fight back from injury for the umpteenth time," he said.
